title: Waveform synthesis harness for continuous batching and queue interaction analysis
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a synthetic arrival waveform generator and load harness ("Waveform Prober") to measure interactions between continuous batching and queueing under realistic mixed workloads. The harness will synthesize multi-tenant arrival traces that combine long-lived sessions, opportunistic microbursts, and background embedding/transcoding traffic. Key outputs: tokens/sec, p95 latency, queue depth distribution, batch size distribution, batching efficiency (tokens_per_batch), KV cache warmup curves, and end-to-end throughput under routing fallbacks. The harness must be configurable (arrival models, token-length distributions, session stickiness, backpressure thresholds) and runnable on our perf testbed and CI smoke nodes.
test_plan: Implement waveform generator with Poisson base + intermittent periodic microbursts + Pareto-heavy tail sessions
Integrate with existing batch/queue simulator (BatchSim v2) to collect batch fill/dispatch timings
Expose experiment matrix via YAML (arrival_rate, microburst_amp, session_pct, kv_hit_rate, concurrency)
Run grid of experiments across model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B) and quantization profiles
Capture metrics to Grafana: tokens/sec, p95, p99, queue_depth_pctiles, batch_size_histogram, tokens_per_batch, kv_cache_hit_ratio
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 4-hour mixed workload trace end-to-end reproducibly
Regression detection: alert if p95 increases by >10% vs baseline over 3 consecutive windows
Batching efficiency measured and stable across three independent runs (stddev <5%)
KV cache warmup curves reproducible and logged
Dashboard with experiment selector and heatmaps delivered
observability_plan: Emit per-join/session traces and metrics with trace_id linking to synthetic session id
Annotate batches with arrival_waveform_tag to filter dashboard
Add control-chart panel for p95 with signal thresholding and auto-alert rule
Store raw experiment traces in s3 at s3://redwood-perf/waveform-prober/<run_id>
risks_and_mitigations: Simulator calibration drift — mitigate by seeding PRNG and publishing seeds with runs
CI resource contention skewing results — use dedicated perf nodes and pre-warm GPUs
KV cache state management complexity — run experiments with controlled cache reset and warmup phases
implementation_notes: Prototype uses waveform-synth python package and BatchSim v2 go harness
Start with single-tenant experiments then expand to multi-tenant by mixing arrival traces
Expose a 'dry-run' mode to validate arrival distributions without GPU execution
